audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim opening historical retelling, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Horeb departure, distributed judges, Kadesh scouting, fear and refusal, wilderness judgment, Moses' exclusion, and failed self-authorized invasion.

verses.restored: These are words Moses spoke to all Israel across Jordan in wilderness, in Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-zahab.

familiar.text: These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain over against the Red sea, between Paran, and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Dizahab.

modern.text: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan—in the Arabah opposite Suph—between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.

original.text: אֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֡ר בָּֽעֲרָבָה֩ מ֨וֹל ס֜וּף בֵּֽין פָּארָ֧ן וּבֵֽין תֹּ֛פֶל וְלָבָ֥ן וַחֲצֵרֹ֖ת וְדִ֥י זָהָֽב

verses.restored: Eleven days from Horeb by way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.

familiar.text: (There are eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of mount Seir unto Kadeshbarnea.)

modern.text: It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of Mount Seir.

original.text: אַחַ֨ד עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ מֵֽחֹרֵ֔ב דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַר שֵׂעִ֑יר עַ֖ד קָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ

verses.restored: In fortieth year, in eleventh month, on first of month, Moses spoke to children of Israel according to all YHWH commanded him for them,

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spake unto the children of Israel, according unto all that the LORD had given him in commandment unto them;

modern.text: In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses proclaimed to the Israelites all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them.

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ בְּאַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֖דֶשׁ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹת֖וֹ אֲלֵהֶֽם

verses.restored: after he struck Sihon king of Amorite dwelling in Heshbon and Og king of Bashan dwelling at Ashtaroth in Edrei.

familiar.text: After he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites, which dwelt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, which dwelt at Astaroth in Edrei:

modern.text: This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and then at Edrei had defeated Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.

original.text: אַחֲרֵ֣י הַכֹּת֗וֹ אֵ֚ת סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וְאֵ֗ת ע֚וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁר יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּעַשְׁתָּרֹ֖ת בְּאֶדְרֶֽעִי

verses.restored: Across Jordan in land of Moab, Moses began to explain this Torah/instruction, saying:

familiar.text: On this side Jordan, in the land of Moab, began Moses to declare this law, saying,

modern.text: On the east side of the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law, saying:

original.text: בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֑ב הוֹאִ֣יל מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֵּאֵ֛ר אֶת הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: YHWH our Divine spoke to us at Horeb, saying, Long enough you have dwelt at this mountain.

familiar.text: The LORD our God spake unto us in Horeb, saying, Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount:

modern.text: The LORD our God said to us at Horeb: “You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

original.text: יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֵ֖ינוּ בְּחֹרֵ֣ב לֵאמֹ֑ר רַב לָכֶ֥ם שֶׁ֖בֶת בָּהָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Turn and set out; go to hill country of Amorite and all its neighbors in Arabah, hill country, Shephelah, Negev, seacoast, land of Canaanite, Lebanon, as far as great river, river Euphrates.

familiar.text: Turn you, and take your journey, and go to the mount of the Amorites, and unto all the places nigh thereunto, in the plain, in the hills, and in the vale, and in the south, and by the sea side, to the land of the Canaanites, and unto Lebanon, unto the great river, the river Euphrates.

modern.text: Resume your journey and go to the hill country of the Amorites; go to all the neighboring peoples in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the foothills, in the Negev, and along the seacoast to the land of the Canaanites and to Lebanon, as far as the great River Euphrates.

original.text: פְּנ֣וּ וּסְע֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם וּבֹ֨אוּ הַ֥ר הָֽאֱמֹרִי֮ וְאֶל כָּל שְׁכֵנָיו֒ בָּעֲרָבָ֥ה בָהָ֛ר וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֥ה וּבַנֶּ֖גֶב וּבְח֣וֹף הַיָּ֑ם אֶ֤רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַלְּבָנ֔וֹן עַד הַנָּהָ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל נְהַר פְּרָֽת

verses.restored: See, I have set land before you. Go in and possess land YHWH swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and their seed after them.

familiar.text: Behold, I have set the land before you: go in and possess the land which the LORD sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and to their seed after them.

modern.text: See, I have placed the land before you. Enter and possess the land that the LORD swore He would give to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.” Moses Appoints Leaders (Exodus 18:13–27)

original.text: רְאֵ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ בֹּ֚אוּ וּרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֣ע יְ֠הוָה לַאֲבֹ֨תֵיכֶ֜ם לְאַבְרָהָ֨ם לְיִצְחָ֤ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב֙ לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֔ם וּלְזַרְעָ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: I spoke to you at that time, saying, I am not able by myself to carry you.

familiar.text: And I spake unto you at that time, saying, I am not able to bear you myself alone:

modern.text: At that time I said to you, “I cannot carry the burden for you alone.

original.text: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא אוּכַ֥ל לְבַדִּ֖י שְׂאֵ֥ת אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: YHWH your Divine has multiplied you, and look, today you are like stars of heavens for multitude.

familiar.text: The LORD your God hath multiplied you, and, behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude.

modern.text: The LORD your God has multiplied you, so that today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky.

original.text: יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם הִרְבָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְהִנְּכֶ֣ם הַיּ֔וֹם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָרֹֽב

verses.restored: May YHWH, Divine of your fathers, add to you a thousand times as many and bless you as he spoke concerning you.

familiar.text: (The LORD God of your fathers make you a thousand times so many more as ye are, and bless you, as he hath promised you!)

modern.text: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times over and bless you as He has promised.

original.text: יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֽוֹתֵכֶ֗ם יֹסֵ֧ף עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם כָּכֶ֖ם אֶ֣לֶף פְּעָמִ֑ים וִיבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: How can I carry by myself your burden, your load, and your disputes?

familiar.text: How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?

modern.text: But how can I bear your troubles, burdens, and disputes all by myself?

original.text: אֵיכָ֥ה אֶשָּׂ֖א לְבַדִּ֑י טָרְחֲכֶ֥ם וּמַֽשַּׂאֲכֶ֖ם וְרִֽיבְכֶֽם

verses.restored: Give for yourselves wise, discerning, and known men from your tribes, and I will set them as your heads.

familiar.text: Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.

modern.text: Choose for yourselves wise, understanding, and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.”

original.text: הָב֣וּ לָ֠כֶם אֲנָשִׁ֨ים חֲכָמִ֧ים וּנְבֹנִ֛ים וִידֻעִ֖ים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶ֑ם וַאֲשִׂימֵ֖ם בְּרָאשֵׁיכֶֽם

verses.restored: You answered me and said, The thing you spoke is good to do.

familiar.text: And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do.

modern.text: And you answered me and said, “What you propose to do is good.”

original.text: וַֽתַּעֲנ֖וּ אֹתִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ טֽוֹב הַדָּבָ֥ר אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת

verses.restored: I took heads of your tribes, wise and known men, and set them as heads over you, leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens, and officers for your tribes.

familiar.text: So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.

modern.text: So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as leaders over you—as commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens, and as officers for your tribes.

original.text: וָאֶקַּ֞ח אֶת רָאשֵׁ֣י שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֗ם אֲנָשִׁ֤ים חֲכָמִים֙ וִֽידֻעִ֔ים וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם רָאשִׁ֖ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם שָׂרֵ֨י אֲלָפִ֜ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֗וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֤י חֲמִשִּׁים֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י עֲשָׂרֹ֔ת וְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: I commanded your judges at that time, saying, Hear between your brothers and judge righteously between man and his brother and his sojourner.

familiar.text: And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.

modern.text: At that time I charged your judges: “Hear the disputes between your brothers, and judge fairly between a man and his brother or a foreign resident.

original.text: וָאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת שֹׁ֣פְטֵיכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁמֹ֤עַ בֵּין אֲחֵיכֶם֙ וּשְׁפַטְתֶּ֣ם צֶ֔דֶק בֵּֽין אִ֥ישׁ וּבֵין אָחִ֖יו וּבֵ֥ין גֵּרֽוֹ

verses.restored: You shall not recognize faces/show partiality in judgment; as small, so great you shall hear. You shall not fear face of man, for judgment is Divine's. The matter too hard for you, bring near to me and I will hear it.

familiar.text: Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.

modern.text: Show no partiality in judging; hear both small and great alike. Do not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God. And bring to me any case too difficult for you, and I will hear it.”

original.text: לֹֽא תַכִּ֨ירוּ פָנִ֜ים בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט כַּקָּטֹ֤ן כַּגָּדֹל֙ תִּשְׁמָע֔וּן לֹ֤א תָג֨וּרוּ֙ מִפְּנֵי אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֥י הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט לֵאלֹהִ֣ים ה֑וּא וְהַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִקְשֶׁ֣ה מִכֶּ֔ם תַּקְרִב֥וּן אֵלַ֖י וּשְׁמַעְתִּֽיו

verses.restored: I commanded you at that time all things you should do.

familiar.text: And I commanded you at that time all the things which ye should do.

modern.text: And at that time I commanded you all the things you were to do. Twelve Spies Sent Out (Numbers 13:1–33)

original.text: וָאֲצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑וא אֵ֥ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן

verses.restored: We set out from Horeb and went through all that great and fearful wilderness you saw, by way of hill country of Amorite, as YHWH our Divine commanded us, and came to Kadesh-barnea.

familiar.text: And when we departed from Horeb, we went through all that great and terrible wilderness, which ye saw by the way of the mountain of the Amorites, as the LORD our God commanded us; and we came to Kadeshbarnea.

modern.text: And just as the LORD our God had commanded us, we set out from Horeb and went toward the hill country of the Amorites, through all the vast and terrifying wilderness you have seen. When we reached Kadesh-barnea,

original.text: וַנִּסַּ֣ע מֵחֹרֵ֗ב וַנֵּ֡לֶךְ אֵ֣ת כָּל הַמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַגָּדוֹל֩ וְהַנּוֹרָ֨א הַה֜וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְאִיתֶ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ הַ֣ר הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ אֹתָ֑נוּ וַנָּבֹ֕א עַ֖ד קָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ

verses.restored: I said to you, You have come to hill country of Amorite, which YHWH our Divine is giving us.

familiar.text: And I said unto you, Ye are come unto the mountain of the Amorites, which the LORD our God doth give unto us.

modern.text: I said: “You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.

original.text: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵכֶ֑ם בָּאתֶם֙ עַד הַ֣ר הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: See, YHWH your Divine has set land before you. Go up, possess, as YHWH Divine of your fathers spoke to you. Do not fear and do not be shattered.

familiar.text: Behold, the LORD thy God hath set the land before thee: go up and possess it, as the LORD God of thy fathers hath said unto thee; fear not, neither be discouraged.

modern.text: See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession of it as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.”

original.text: רְ֠אֵה נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ לְפָנֶ֖יךָ אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ עֲלֵ֣ה רֵ֗שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ לָ֔ךְ אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָֽת

verses.restored: All of you came near to me and said, Let us send men before us, and they shall search out land for us and return word concerning way by which we should go up and cities into which we should come.

familiar.text: And ye came near unto me every one of you, and said, We will send men before us, and they shall search us out the land, and bring us word again by what way we must go up, and into what cities we shall come.

modern.text: Then all of you approached me and said, “Let us send men ahead of us to search out the land and bring us word of what route to follow and which cities to enter.”

original.text: וַתִּקְרְב֣וּן אֵלַי֮ כֻּלְּכֶם֒ וַתֹּאמְר֗וּ נִשְׁלְחָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ וְיַחְפְּרוּ לָ֖נוּ אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיָשִׁ֤בוּ אֹתָ֨נוּ֙ דָּבָ֔ר אֶת הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲלֶה בָּ֔הּ וְאֵת֙ הֶֽעָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָבֹ֖א אֲלֵיהֶֽן

verses.restored: The thing was good in my eyes, and I took twelve men from you, one man from each tribe.

familiar.text: And the saying pleased me well: and I took twelve men of you, one of a tribe:

modern.text: The plan seemed good to me, so I selected twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.

original.text: וַיִּיטַ֥ב בְּעֵינַ֖י הַדָּבָ֑ר וָאֶקַּ֤ח מִכֶּם֙ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲנָשִׁ֔ים אִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד לַשָּֽׁבֶט

verses.restored: They turned and went up hill country and came to wadi of Eshcol and scouted it.

familiar.text: And they turned and went up into the mountain, and came unto the valley of Eshcol, and searched it out.

modern.text: They left and went up into the hill country, and came to the Valley of Eshcol and spied out the land.

original.text: וַיִּפְנוּ֙ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ הָהָ֔רָה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד נַ֣חַל אֶשְׁכֹּ֑ל וַֽיְרַגְּל֖וּ אֹתָֽהּ

verses.restored: They took in their hands from fruit of land and brought it down to us and returned word, saying, Good is land YHWH our Divine is giving us.

familiar.text: And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and brought us word again, and said, It is a good land which the LORD our God doth give us.

modern.text: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands, carried it down to us, and brought us word: “It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us.” Israel’s Rebellion (Numbers 14:1–12)

original.text: וַיִּקְח֤וּ בְיָדָם֙ מִפְּרִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיּוֹרִ֖דוּ אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וַיָּשִׁ֨בוּ אֹתָ֤נוּ דָבָר֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ טוֹבָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: But you were unwilling to go up and rebelled against mouth/command of YHWH your Divine.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the LORD your God:

modern.text: But you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.

translation_notes: Deuteronomy begins as Moses' retrospective interpretation, not a neutral transcript; comparison with Exodus and Numbers is essential.
Judicial leadership is distributed because one person cannot carry communal burden alone.
Judges are commanded to hear small and great, Israelite and sojourner, without partiality.
The scouting crisis distinguishes observed difficulty from fear-amplifying rhetoric and self-perception.
The failed invasion is explicitly unauthorized: confession does not make violence obedient when YHWH has said not to go.
Land-gift and conquest language is ancient covenant rhetoric and must not authorize modern colonial claims or displacement.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 1 to sanctify conquest, militarized obedience, authoritarian leadership, or blame children for ancestral failure. Its constructive movements are distributed judgment, equal hearing, honest memory, and refusal to call self-authorized violence faith.
